title: North Qatar Half-Day Private Tour
imageAlt: Al Zubarah Fort, a restored white fortification in northern Qatar, under a clear sky
summary: A private half-day run up Qatar's quiet northern coast: the UNESCO-listed Al Zubarah Fort, the mangrove boardwalk at Purple Island and the fishing harbour at Al Khor, all arranged from your door.
overview: Head north from Doha and Qatar opens into coastline, mangroves and an old UNESCO World Heritage trading town — the half of the country most visitors never reach. This private tour devotes the day to it, with an air-conditioned vehicle, Wi-Fi on board and a guide who stays with your group only, so each stop lasts as long as you like. The drive takes about an hour and a half through desert and coastal plain before the whitewashed walls of Al Zubarah Fort, a restored garrison beside the ruins of the old pearling town. From there, a wooden walkway carries you out among the mangroves of Purple Island, and Al Khor's corniche makes the final picture beside a harbour of working dhows.
bestFor: History seekers, nature lovers and photographers
highlights: Al Zubarah Fort and its UNESCO World Heritage site
Al Khor harbour and seaside corniche

itinerary.title: Pickup in Doha
itinerary.description: Your guide and driver collect you from your hotel lobby, the arrivals gate at Hamad International Airport or Doha Cruise Terminal 1, and settle you into an air-conditioned vehicle with Wi-Fi on board. The drive north takes about an hour and a half across desert and coastal plain.

itinerary.title: Al Zubarah Fort
itinerary.description: Step inside the restored fort with its circular corner towers and small museum, standing beside the UNESCO-listed archaeological site of the old trading town of Al Zubarah. Your guide shares the pearling-port story while you explore at your own pace.

itinerary.title: Purple Island mangroves
itinerary.description: A wooden walkway leads through mangroves and shallow lagoons rich with birdlife at Jazirat Bin Ghanim. There is time to wander the boardwalk, watch for herons and take in the quiet water before moving on.

itinerary.title: Al Khor fishing harbour
itinerary.description: Pause by the water at this old pearling town, where fishing dhows bob at their moorings along a seaside corniche. It is a short, easy stop suited to photographs and a last look at the coast.

itinerary.title: Coastal drive back
itinerary.description: Board the vehicle for the return leg toward Doha, with a rest break along the way if you need one. Flexible timing keeps it relaxed whichever stops ran long.

itinerary.title: Drop-off wherever suits you
itinerary.description: Return to your hotel, the airport or the cruise terminal about five hours after pickup. Mornings beat the heat and late afternoons catch the coast in softer light — pick whichever departure fits your day.

included: Pickup and drop-off at your hotel, Hamad International Airport or Doha Cruise Terminal
Private air-conditioned vehicle, your party only
Flexible time at every stop — the vehicle waits while you explore
notes: Plan for about five hours door to door; the stop order and exact departure time shift with the season to make the most of daylight and cooler hours.
Purple Island involves a walk along a boardwalk with little shade, so wear comfortable shoes and bring sun protection.
High tides or occasional maintenance can change the Purple Island walk; the guide adjusts the route and keeps you on safe footing when it does.
Groups larger than six travel in additional vehicles rather than being mixed with other parties.
Infants under 3 ride along at no charge, and cancellations are accepted up to 24 hours before departure.

faqs.question: Where does the tour pick me up and drop me off?
faqs.answer: From your hotel lobby in Doha, directly from arrivals gate 4 at Hamad International Airport, or from Doha Cruise Terminal 1. At the end we return you to whichever of those three suits you best.

faqs.question: Is this a private tour or shared with other travellers?
faqs.answer: Fully private — the vehicle and guide are for your group only. Parties larger than six simply travel in additional vehicles so everyone stays together.

faqs.question: How long do we spend at each stop?
faqs.answer: Roughly an hour and a half at the fort, two hours at Purple Island and about half an hour at Al Khor, plus the drives in between. Because it is private, the timing flexes to how long you want to linger.

faqs.question: Is there much walking involved?
faqs.answer: Most of the walking is on Purple Island, where a wooden boardwalk carries you through the mangroves. The fort and the Al Khor corniche are short, flat walks, so the day suits most fitness levels.

faqs.question: When is the best time of year for this route?
faqs.answer: October to April is ideal, with mild weather that makes time outdoors at the fort and the island comfortable. In the hotter months we start earlier so you see the sights before midday.

faqs.question: What happens if the weather turns?
faqs.answer: If high tide, strong winds or extreme heat make an outdoor stop unwise, the guide adjusts the route and the order of stops and talks you through the alternatives before setting out.

sampleReviews.name: Hannah W.
sampleReviews.title: The quiet half of Qatar
sampleReviews.text: Al Zubarah Fort felt like discovering a place all to ourselves, and the mangrove boardwalk at Purple Island was the surprise of our trip. Our guide kept everything flexible so we could linger where we liked.

sampleReviews.name: Rakesh P.
sampleReviews.title: A great break from the city
sampleReviews.text: Five hours flew by in a comfortable car with Wi-Fi and a guide who knew the story of the old pearling ports. The Al Khor harbour stop was worth the drive alone.
